newsitem.title: GERMANY: ERM open to Italian return at right time - Germany.
newsitem.headline: ERM open to Italian return at right time - Germany.

text.p: Germany would welcome Italy back as a partner into the European Exchange Rate Mechanism once terms and timing have been agreed, a Finance Ministry spokesman said on Tuesday.
"Naturally the ERM is open to all European Union members, and as many member states should take part as possible as long as the timing is right," the spokesman told Reuters.

Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said in Rome that talks on restoring the Italian lira to the European currency grid -- membership of which is a precondition of joining the launch of a single currency -- could start at any time.

Prodi's comments followed an unsourced Italian newspaper report which said both Germany and France were seeking to delay a quick return of the lira because speculation in Italian bond futures could unravel nastily and knock the lira's value.
The lira, ejected from the ERM under speculative attack back in 1992, rose to 1,006.50/85 to the German mark on Tuesday against 1,007.50/85 at the start of the week.
There has been concern among countries in the hard currency core of Europe that Italy could lock in competitive gains from the lira devaluation if it returned to the ERM too soon.
